question: The Visuddhimagga, a key Buddhist text, was written by which of the following scholars?
solution: The correct answer is __**Buddhaghosa**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • **The Visuddhimagga**, meaning "The Path of Purification," is a key text in **Buddhist literature**. It serves as an encyclopedic guide to the practice of Theravāda Buddhism. • This text was composed by the renowned scholar-monk **Buddhaghosa** in the **5th century CE**. *Hence, the correct answer is Buddhaghosa.* • **Buddhaghosa** was a commentator and translator who played a crucial role in systematizing and preserving the teachings of Theravāda Buddhism. His work is highly regarded in the Theravāda tradition. • The **Visuddhimagga** is divided into three main sections, corresponding to the threefold training in Buddhism: **Sīla (morality), Samādhi (concentration), and Paññā (wisdom).** • It provides detailed instructions on meditation, the interpretation of the Buddha's teachings, and the attainment of **nirvana**. • The text is based on the Pāli Canon, the foundational scripture of Theravāda Buddhism, and serves as a comprehensive manual for Buddhist practitioners. • The **Visuddhimagga** is highly influential and remains a cornerstone of Theravāda monastic education and spiritual practice. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __ • **Buddhaghosa and His Contributions:** • **Buddhaghosa** was an Indian Theravāda Buddhist commentator who lived in the **5th century CE**. He is considered one of the most significant figures in the history of Theravāda Buddhism. • He traveled to **Sri Lanka**, where he studied the Pāli Canon and commentaries preserved in the Mahāvihāra monastery. • Buddhaghosa's primary goal was to systematize and translate the extensive Buddhist teachings from **Sinhalese** into **Pāli**, thereby preserving them for future generations. • **The Structure of Visuddhimagga:** • The text is divided into three sections: • **Sīla**: Focuses on ethical conduct and discipline for laypersons and monastics. • **Samādhi**: Explains meditation techniques, including the **jhana** states (levels of meditative absorption). • **Paññā**: Discusses wisdom, particularly insights into the nature of reality, impermanence, and the path to **nirvana**. • The text also includes commentaries on various aspects of the **Buddha's teachings**, making it an essential guide for practitioners and scholars. • **Key Features of the Visuddhimagga:** • The **Visuddhimagga** is considered a **practical guide** to meditation and ethical conduct, offering detailed instructions on achieving liberation. • It bridges the gap between the theoretical teachings of the **Pāli Canon** and their application in everyday practice. • The text is revered not only in **Sri Lanka** but also in other Theravāda Buddhist countries, such as **Thailand, Myanmar, and Cambodia.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** • **Contributions of Other Scholars:** • **Nagarjuna**: A key figure in Mahayana Buddhism, he is credited with founding the **Madhyamaka** school of thought, emphasizing the concept of **śūnyatā (emptiness).** • **Aryadeva**: A disciple of Nagarjuna, he expanded on the teachings of the Madhyamaka school and wrote influential texts such as **Four Hundred Verses.** • **Vasubandhu**: A prominent scholar in Mahayana Buddhism, he co-founded the **Yogacara** school and authored influential works like the **Abhidharmakośa.** • **Significance of the Visuddhimagga:** • The **Visuddhimagga** remains a cornerstone of Theravāda Buddhist practice and scholarship, providing a comprehensive framework for achieving spiritual liberation. • It is widely studied and respected in Buddhist monastic education systems across Theravāda countries. bc:T3355,
